n: Samuel continues: unless the Nephites repent, their homes will be left empty and ruined. Jesus used the same phrase about Jerusalem.

f.w: your houses shall be left unto you desolate

n: He describes the suffering of war in human terms: nursing mothers and pregnant women unable to flee, trampled and left to die. It echoes Jesus’s warnings about Jerusalem’s fall.

f.w: wo unto them which are with child

n: The Nephites have been the Lord’s chosen people. He loved them, and because He loved them, He corrected them during their times of sin.

f.w: chastened them because he loveth them

n: By contrast, the Lord “hated” the Lamanites’ evil deeds, which came from false traditions. Yet salvation reached them through Nephite preaching, and for that purpose God prolonged their lives. God’s rejection was of their deeds, not of them as people.

f.g: In Hebrew idiom, often means “rejected” or “loved less,” here tied to their evil deeds.

n: Most Lamanites are now on the path of duty, living carefully before God and keeping His commandments under the law of Moses.

f.g: Carefully, watchfully, with attention to every step.

n: They work tirelessly to bring the rest of their people to the truth, and new converts join daily.
The Nephites have seen it themselves: Lamanites who learn the truth and believe the scriptures and prophets are led to faith in the Lord and repentance, which bring a change of heart.
Those who reach this point are firm and steadfast in the faith and in the freedom it gives.
The Nephites also know these converts buried their weapons and would rather be killed than risk sinning by shedding blood. Their faith in Christ shows in their fear of sin.
Because they stay firm once enlightened, the Lord will bless them and prolong their days, despite their failings.
Even if they later fall away in unbelief, the Lord will preserve them until the time foretold by Zenos and other prophets when the Lamanites will be restored to the truth.

f.w: the restoration of our brethren, the Lamanites

n: In the last days the Lord’s promises extend to the Lamanites. Although they will be driven, hunted, and scattered, the Lord will be merciful to them.
Prophecy says they will again come to know their Redeemer, the true Shepherd, and be counted among His sheep. The Book of Mormon itself was written partly for this purpose.
So, unless the Nephites repent, things will go better for the Lamanites than for them.

f.w: better for them than for you

n: If the Lamanites had seen the miracles the Nephites have seen, they would never have fallen into unbelief. Greater light brings greater responsibility.

f.w: had the mighty works been shown unto them

n: So the Lord promises not to destroy the Lamanites completely; in His own time they will return to Him.

f.w: in the day of my wisdom
f.g: At the time God judges best.

n: But the Nephites, if they won’t repent, will be utterly destroyed for their unbelief despite all God’s mighty works. This came true about four centuries later.
